1o0s9j3:1427: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Adds Quality Evaluation and Policy Control for Deploying Trustworthy AI Agents by Danilo Poccia on 02 December 2025 in Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Machine Learning, Announcements, Artificial Intelligence, AWS re:Invent, Generative AI, Launch, News Permalink Share Today, we are excited to announce new features in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to further remove the barriers to taking AI agents into production. Organizations across industries are already building solutions on AgentCore, the state-of-the-art platform to securely build, deploy, and run powerful agents at any scale. In just five months since the preview launch, the AgentCore SDK has been downloaded more than 2 million times. For example, PGA TOUR, a pioneer and innovation leader in sports, has built a multi-agent content generation system to write articles for its digital platforms. The new solution built on AgentCore increases content writing speed by 1000% and reduces costs by 95%, enabling PGA TOUR to provide comprehensive coverage of every athlete in the field. Independent software vendors (ISVs) such as Workday are building the future of software on AgentCore. The AgentCore code interpreter provides Workday planning agents with secure data protection and essential capabilities for financial data exploration. Users can analyze financial and operational data through natural language queries, making financial planning intuitive and self-directed. This feature reduces time spent on routine planning analysis by 30%, saving approximately 100 hours per month. Brazilian distributor and retailer Grupo Elfa relies on AgentCore observability to achieve full audit traceability and real-time metric monitoring of its agents, turning reactive processes into proactive operations. With this unified platform, their sales team can process thousands of quotes daily while the organization maintains full visibility into agent decisions, helping achieve 100% traceability of agent decisions and interactions and reducing issue resolution time by 50%. As organizations scale their agent deployments, they face challenges in implementing the right guardrails and quality checks to deploy agents with confidence. The very autonomy that makes agents powerful also makes them difficult to deploy at scale with confidence, as they may improperly access sensitive data, make unauthorized decisions, or take unexpected actions. Development teams must strike a balance: enabling agent autonomy while ensuring agents operate within acceptable boundaries, and also meeting the high quality bar required to put agents in front of customers and employees. The new capabilities announced today remove the guesswork from this process, helping you build and deploy trustworthy AI agents with confidence: Policy in AgentCore (Preview): Use policies with fine-grained permissions to intercept tool calls at the AgentCore gateway before they run, defining clear boundaries for agent actions. AgentCore Evaluations (Preview): Monitor agent quality based on actual behavior, using built-in evaluators (for dimensions such as correctness and usefulness) and custom evaluators (for business-specific requirements). We are also introducing capabilities that expand what agents can do: Episodic memory in AgentCore: A new long-term capability that helps agents learn from experience and adapt solutions in similar situations, improving consistency and performance on future similar tasks. Bidirectional streaming in AgentCore runtime: Deploy voice agents where both the user and the agent can speak simultaneously in a natural conversational flow.
1pn5zlh:269: AgentCore Evaluations provides fully managed continuous evaluation capabilities that monitor agent performance based on actual behavior. Built-in evaluators cover dimensions such as correctness, usefulness, tool selection accuracy, safety, goal success rate, and context relevance; custom evaluators allow scoring criteria to be tailored to business requirements. The core value of this design lies in extending quality assessment from the "testing phase" to the "production phase," forming a continuous monitoring loop. Evaluation results integrate with CloudWatch, supporting alerts and automated responses. When quality metrics fall below thresholds—for example, a decline in customer service agent satisfaction or a drop of more than 10% in politeness score within 8 hours—the system can immediately trigger alerts. This marks a paradigm shift from reactive detection to proactive monitoring.

9sby1y:321: AgentCore policies support two creation methods: natural language description and direct use of the Cedar policy language. Cedar is an open-source executable policy language from AWS that provides fine-grained permission controls. The elegance of this design is that natural language policy generation is not simple LLM translation—it understands the tool structure and generates syntactically correct, semantically consistent policies, and can automatically identify conditions that are too permissive, too restrictive, or unsatisfiable. From an engineering practice perspective, this "natural language → Cedar automatic reasoning and validation" workflow significantly lowers the barrier to policy authoring, enabling development, security, and compliance teams to collaboratively create and audit rules without requiring specialized Cedar expertise. The policy engine integrates with the AgentCore gateway to intercept tool calls as they occur, processing requests while maintaining operational speed—a low-latency approach to embedding security controls in the data plane.

f4wqtj:302: The article reveals the core challenge enterprises face when deploying AI agents at scale: the fundamental contradiction between the powerful autonomy of agents and their safe, controllable operation. Agents may improperly access sensitive data, make unauthorized decisions, or take unexpected actions, forcing development teams to balance enabling agent autonomy with ensuring agents operate within acceptable boundaries. The essence of this contradiction lies in the fact that traditional software security models are based on deterministic rules, while AI agent behavior is emergent and uncertain, requiring a new governance paradigm. AgentCore's policy mechanism treats agents as "autonomous actors" whose decisions must be validated before gaining access to tools, systems, or data—an "externalized" security control approach decoupled from the agent's own reasoning loop. This design philosophy decouples security boundary definition from agent implementation, enabling consistent governance across models and architectures.
